Hi Alex --

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on related to encryption and key management:

Highlights from the call:
- FinCorp is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing assistants that will process PII (names, account numbers).
- Key concerns: in-transit and at-rest encryption, customer-managed key (CMK) support, HSM/BYOK options, and whether logs might contain PII.
- Regulatory note: you asked about data residency for EU-based customers later in the rollout.

Action items we covered:
1) I'll send a short note summarizing our encryption options and how CMK/BYOK works (this thread).
2) We'll schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev to walk through a KMS integration and architecture (I suggested Tuesday or Wednesday next week).
3) Rishi will share a draft mutual action plan + timeline and the initial commercial terms.

Short answers up-front (details below):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ / TLS 1.3 by default. Private deployments support mTLS.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for storage; model KV caches and tokens encrypted at rest.
- CMK: Supported on Hosted (integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault for encrypted payloads/objects) and fully supported in Private (BYOK/HSM attachments).
- Logs: Audit logs are available; sensitive fields can be redacted or routed to customer-managed logging solutions.

I've attached our KMS architecture diagram and a SOC 2 summary. Below I'll expand a bit on the most common questions you asked so your security and engineering teams have something to reference.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa --

Thanks for the quick recap -- that helps. A few clarifying questions from our security and infra leads before we set the deep-dive:

1) In-transit: do you enforce TLS 1.3 by default for hosted API traffic? Is there support for mTLS on the hosted offering or only for Dedicated/Private?

2) At-rest: you mentioned AES-256 -- can you confirm which components are encrypted with customer-managed keys vs platform-managed keys (e.g., object store vs KV cache vs long-term logs)?

3) CMK/Key lifecycle: does Redwood have access to plaintext if we use CMK? How is key rotation handled and can we push rotations from our KMS?

4) HSM/BYOK: for Private deployments, do you support FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs? Can we bring our own HSM or do you host an HSM in our VPC?

5) Logging: our compliance team wants to know if logs ever include unredacted PII by default (we prefer logs to be PII-free and full payloads not to be stored). What redaction controls are available and can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog)?

6) Data residency: for EU customers, can keys and at-rest data be kept strictly in eu-west-1? Same question for backup retention locations.

If you can provide short bullet answers for each and point us to any docs or SOC evidence, that would be great.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Security 
FinCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Alex --

Thanks -- answers to your questions below (brief + pragmatic). I've also attached a one-pager KMS integration checklist and the SOC 2 summary we shared earlier. Happy to expand any item on the call with Dev.

1) In-transit:
- Hosted API: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported; we have TLS 1.3 across our fleet and are progressively enforcing TLS 1.3 for new clients.
- mTLS: available for Dedicated and Private deployments (mTLS for Hosted is available via private peering and VPN arrangements; generally used in Dedicated/Private).

2) At-rest (what can be CMK vs platform-managed):
- Object store (customer data blobs) -- can be encrypted with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) on Hosted when configured via tenant-level CMK.
- KV cache and ephemeral model caches -- encrypted at rest with AES-256. For Hosted, these are platform-managed by default; for Dedicated/Private we offer options to use CMK-backed encryption for persisted caches.
- Persistent logs/audit: platform retains structured audit logs; we can optionally redact payload fields and/or stream logs to your SIEM where you control retention.

3) CMK / key lifecycle:
- Redwood does not retain plaintext of customer-encrypted objects when you use CMK for object storage -- keys remain in customer KMS and Redwood stores references/encrypted envelopes.
- Key rotation: we support rotation schedules on the customer KMS side; Redwood will fetch new envelopes as keys rotate and supports automated re-encryption workflows for persisted objects when needed.
- Access: we do not have administrative access to your CMKs. For Hosted CMK integrations we rely on customer-managed KMS permissions (we require the minimal set of KMS decrypt/encrypt IAM permissions).

4) HSM / BYOK for Private: 
- For Private deployments we support FIPS 140-2/3-compliant HSMs and BYOK patterns. Options: (a) customer-provisioned HSM in their VPC that Redwood integrates with, or (b) Redwood-managed HSM appliance colocated in the customer environment (per contract).
- We can discuss specific HSM vendors (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) during the technical deep-dive.

5) Logging and PII controls:
- Default: structured audit logs do not persist full request payloads; we capture metadata (request id, timestamps, model, tokens generated).
- Redaction: configurable at ingestion -- you can request full payload redaction or field-level redaction rules.
- Log forwarding: yes -- we can stream audit logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/Elastic) over secure connectors. Once routed, retention is controlled by your SIEM or storage.

6) Data residency:
- Hosted: we support region-specific deployment to keep data and keys in eu-west-1 for EU customers. Backups and snapshots can be restricted to the selected region on request.
- Private: fully customer-controlled (keys and data do not leave your network unless explicitly configured).

Next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with Dev Patel to go over the KMS flow and architecture (I've proposed times in the calendar link below).
- Rishi will follow up with the MAP and initial commercial terms.

Links / attachments: KMS architecture diagram (attached), KMS integration checklist (attached), SOC 2 summary (attached), KMS docs: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/kms-overview

If you want, I can also put our security architect on the call for the HSM/BYOK discussion. What time works on Tuesday 12/6 or Wednesday 12/7?

Best,
